title: Open v0.11 continuation and execution-efficiency discovery
rationale: v0.10 proved end-to-end deterministic orchestration but its retrospective identified continuation friction, while the promoted v0.08 task compiler already exposes conservative dependency and parallel-safety structure. The highest-leverage next step is to combine package-only continuation with a governed execution-efficiency architecture so future specs optimize time-to-verified-implementation through algorithm simplification, useful safe parallelism, latency management, partitioning, minimal context/I/O, dependency/critical-path analysis, load balancing, reuse, safe preparation, failure isolation, and explicit integration contracts. This is opened as unfrozen discovery so metrics and evidence rules can be preregistered before implementation.
constraints: All v0.10 frozen contract-bound artifacts and earlier frozen/failed release history remain immutable.
v0.11 remains unfrozen discovery; this decision does not authorize implementation or release freeze.
Efficiency optimization is subordinate to correctness, safety, traceability, reproducibility, verification independence, and governance.
Parallelism must be evidence-backed and must not be inflated through arbitrary task fragmentation or invented independence.
Empirical wall-clock, provider, context, or compute savings may not be claimed from structural/synthetic evidence alone.
Before v0.11 freeze, exact baselines, schemas, fixtures, denominators, thresholds, guardrails, immutable boundaries, and parent preflight must be explicit and validation-clean.
